news.titleTr: CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9325-26 CFTC Files Lawsuit Against Arkansas as the Agency Defends its Federal Jurisdiction Over Prediction Markets November 13, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced that it has filed a lawsuit against Arkansas to block the state’s attempts to halt event-contract trading and impose up to hundreds of millions of dollars in civil penalties on CFTC-registered exchanges. Arkansas is bringing a civil enforcement against Kalshi in state court, a CFTC-designated contract market. Arkansas’s efforts to obstruct the functions of CFTC-registered exchanges operating lawfully under the Commodity Exchange Act are preempted by federal law. “As prediction markets continue to prove their value in being useful for risk management and providing the public with valuable information about the future, Arkansas seeks to shut down event contracts ranging from sports and politics to other important world events,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “The CFTC will continue to defend its sole jurisdiction over these federally regulated markets as granted by Congress under the Commodity Exchange Act, and the Commission will not let state interference thwart its regulatory efforts and destroy federally regulated markets.” Arkansas is the 11th state the CFTC has sued to vindicate federal sovereign interests. The CFTC has also submitted amicus briefs in four federal Courts of Appeal and one state Supreme Court. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers
news.articleText: Release Number 9324-26 CFTC Sanctions Eight Individuals for Acting as Unregistered Associated Persons of Foreign Introducing Brokers November 09, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced eight orders filing and settling charges against Michael Talento, Anthony Tyler Williams, Quillan Roberto Black, Christopher Williams, Michael Levi Peters, Jordan Taylor Morgan, Lewis Matthew Neal, and Tyler Evan MacKechnie for acting as unregistered associated persons of unregistered foreign introducing brokers. According to the orders, the introducing brokers engaged in the solicitation of orders for off-exchange leveraged or margined retail foreign currency and retail commodities transactions with U.S. customers who were not eligible contract participants. The respondents solicited those customers without registering as associated persons of the introducing brokers, as required. Under the orders, the respondents must cease and desist from engaging in their illegal conduct. They also are barred for two years from registering with the Commission in any capacity or acting as a principal, agent, or employee of any CFTC registrant. Each order also recognizes the penalty the respondent owes in a related Securities and Exchange Commission proceeding. These orders relate to a prior Commission order sanctioning Netrios LP Ltd. and Red Acre Ltd. for facilitating illegal off-exchange commodity transactions with U.S. customers. [See CFTC Press Release No. 9263-26] The SEC has filed and settled charges against the respondents based on the same underlying conduct. The CFTC thanks the SEC for its assistance. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation
news.articleText: Release Number 9323-26 CFTC Issues Impartial Access Requirements Interpretation November 05, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an interpretation (“Interpretation”) of the requirement that designated contract markets (“DCMs”) provide competitive, open, fair, and impartial access to their members and persons with trading privileges under Commission Regulation 38.151(b) (“Impartial Access Requirements”). “Derivatives markets must operate on a uniform basis at a national scale in order to achieve the purposes set out in the Commodity Exchange Act,” said Chairman Michael S. Selig. “Geographic access restrictions are inconsistent with those purposes and the Act’s impartial access requirements.” DCMs must cease domestic geographic restrictions that violate the Impartial Access Requirements within 30 days, or else submit to the Division of Market Oversight (“Division”) an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. Further, within 30 days, DCMs should ensure that intermediaries accessing their markets are not impeding and are complying with the DCM’s Impartial Access Requirements, or else submit to the Division an explanation for why such compliance is not feasible. The Commission will consider the facts and circumstances of any particular case in connection with potential Commission action. -CFTC-

According to the letter, a derivatives clearing organization may use a trust company for daily settlements if it treats the trust company as it would a settlement bank under applicable CFTC requirements. -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets
news.articleText: Release Number 9321-26 CFTC and USDA Sign MOU to Protect Integrity of American Agricultural Markets November 04, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission and the U.S. Department of Agriculture today announced their signing of a Memorandum of Understanding intended to safeguard the integrity of U.S. agricultural markets. The MOU will allow the CFTC and USDA to harmonize policies and practices to better share information and increase access to risk management tools. The agreement will also assist both agencies with monitoring and identifying structural or potential systematic risks, among other things. “For decades, America’s agricultural community has relied on our markets to hedge risk, manage uncertainty, and plan for the future,” said CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig. “I’m proud that the CFTC and USDA have formalized this partnership through an MOU that will strengthen protections for America’s farmers, ranchers, and producers while expanding opportunities to manage risk through more efficient data sharing. I commend Secretary Rollins for her partnership and commitment to a more coordinated regulatory approach that safeguards the integrity of our markets and ensures they continue serving the agricultural community that feeds and clothes our nation.” “Faster and more transparent data sharing between USDA and CFTC is critical to helping our farmers and ranchers navigate an ever-changing market,” said USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins. “This MOU builds upon USDA’s ongoing data modernization efforts and allows our agencies to collaboratively identify risks and improve responses to market events. Breaking down barriers between government agencies to deliver for our customers is a hallmark of this administration and I am looking forward to the successes this MOU will bring.” -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud
news.articleText: Release Number 9320-26 CFTC Secures Court Order Directing Texas Man and His Company to Pay Over $13 Million in Commodities Fraud November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today announced the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Texas entered a default judgment against defendants Walter Dunning Larrick III and Cambridge Financial Advisors LLC for their participation in a commodities fraud scheme. In entering the default judgment, the court found the defendants fraudulently solicited and misappropriated more than $3 million from participants. The court found the defendants falsely represented they would use participant funds to trade futures and options, including those involving natural gas, oil, and gold; made material misrepresentations and omissions about the profitability of commodity trading with them; and issued false account statements to conceal their misconduct. The court further found the defendants misappropriated participant funds by making payments to existing participants in a manner akin to a Ponzi scheme, paying Larrick’s personal expenses, and sending funds to offshore accounts in Costa Rica. The court ordered the defendants to pay a $9,767,625 civil monetary penalty and $3,255,875 in restitution. It also permanently enjoined them from further violations of the Commodity Exchange Act and Commission regulations, as charged, and imposed permanent trading and registration bans. The default judgment resolves all claims in the CFTC’s 2023 complaint. [See CFTC Press Release No. 8768-23.] -CFTC-

news.title: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.verification: Birincil kaynak
news.titleTr: CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures
news.articleText: Release Number 9319-26 CFTC Chairman Selig Releases Statement on Equity Perpetual Futures November 03, 2026 WASHINGTON — CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig today released a statement announcing that perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities can begin trading for the first time on designated contract markets that are dually registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission as notice-registered national securities exchanges to trade security futures products. Key excerpts from Chairman Selig’s statement: “Today, perpetual futures contracts on individual equity securities (the ‘Equity Perps’) can begin trading for the first time on CFTC-registered exchanges. … “This expansion marks a significant step towards allowing U.S. market participants, consistent with applicable law, to avail themselves of the advantages of perpetual futures that have led to their emergence as widely sought tools for risk-management and price-discovery. I believe that bringing these types of innovative products into our regulated markets ensures that American investors and traders can access these products within the protections of the CFTC’s proven regulatory framework, rather than being forced to turn to offshore, and often unregulated, venues. … “The Equity Perps build on the foundation of the [Commodity Futures Modernization Act of 2000] and the [CFTC-SEC Memorandum of Understanding]. For too long, regulatory uncertainty left innovative products, such as security futures and equity perpetual futures, stranded in what SEC Chairman Paul S. Atkins has aptly described as a regulatory ‘no man’s land’ due to a lack of harmonization between the agencies. The CFTC and SEC have turned the page on that era, and are committed to delivering regulatory clarity for innovative products and a clear path to market, rather than more casualties of jurisdictional disputes.” Read Chairman Selig’s full statement here. -CFTC-

items.articleText: Okullarda yeni dönem: MEB'den sınavlarda yapay zeka adımı - Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB), ölçme ve değerlendirme yönetmeliğinde değişikliğe gitti. Yeni düzenlemeyle sınav sorularının hazırlanması ve değerlendirilmesinde yapay zeka araçları kullanılabilecek. Ortak yazılı sınavlara ilişkin kurallar da yeniden belirlendi. Milli Eğitim Bakanlığı (MEB), Ölçme ve Değerlendirme Yönetmeliği'nde değişikliğe gitti. Yeni düzenlemeyle okul öncesi ve ilkokullarda sınav yapılamayacağı hükme bağlanırken, ortak yazılı sınavların uygulanmasına ilişkin esaslar yeniden belirlendi. Soru hazırlama ve değerlendirme süreçlerinde yapay zeka kullanımının da önü açıldı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Resmi Gazete'de yayımlanan yönetmelik değişikliğiyle, MEB'e bağlı resmi ve özel eğitim kurumlarında yürütülen ölçme ve değerlendirme faaliyetleri, merkezi sistem sınavları ile ulusal ve uluslararası izleme araştırmalarına ilişkin yeni kurallar belirlendi. Düzenlemeye göre ölçme ve değerlendirme faaliyetleri, öğrencilerin öğrenme süreçlerindeki gelişimlerinin izlenmesi, ihtiyaçlarının belirlenmesi ve öğretim süreçlerinin geliştirilmesi amacıyla yürütülecek. İlkokullarda sınav yapılmayacak Yönetmelikte öne çıkan düzenlemelerden biri okul öncesi ve ilkokullara ilişkin oldu. Bu eğitim kademelerinde herhangi bir ad altında sınav yapılamayacak. Öğrencilerin bilişsel, fiziksel, sosyal ve duygusal gelişimleri eğitim süreci boyunca takip edilecek ve desteklenecek. Öğrenci başarısı ise öğretim programındaki öğrenme çıktıları ve kazanımlar esas alınarak yapılan ölçme ve değerlendirme uygulamalarından elde edilen sonuçlara göre belirlenecek. Sınav sonuçları sıralama için kullanılamayacak Ölçme ve değerlendirme uygulamalarından elde edilen sonuçlar, öğrenciler, sınıflar, okullar veya iller arasında sıralama, karşılaştırma ya da kıyaslama yapmak amacıyla kullanılamayacak. Sınav, ölçme, değerlendirme ve yerleştirme işlemleri güvenilirlik, gizlilik ve tarafsızlık ilkeleri çerçevesinde gerçekleştirilecek. Sınavlarda yapay zeka dönemi Yeni yönetmelikle eğitimde dijitalleşmeye yönelik de önemli bir adım atıldı. Ölçme ve değerlendirme faaliyetleri, Bakanlığın uygun gördüğü dijital sistemler ve araçlarla kısmen veya tamamen elektronik ortamda yürütülebilecek. Soru hazırlama ve değerlendirme süreçlerini desteklemek, bu süreçlerin etkinliğini artırmak amacıyla MEB tarafından uygun görülen yapay zeka araçları kullanılabilecek. Sınav tarihleri e-Okul üzerinden duyurulacak Okullarda yapılacak sınavlar, Bakanlık tarafından belirlenen takvime göre gerçekleştirilecek. Sınav tarihleri öğretim yılı başında okullar tarafından e-Okul üzerinden ilan edilecek. Mücbir sebepler nedeniyle sınavların belirlenen tarihlerde yapılamaması halinde valilikler sınav tarihlerini değiştirebilecek. Bazı mesleki ve teknik ortaöğretim kurumları ile mesleki eğitim merkezlerinde ise sınav tarihleri ilgili okul veya kurumlar tarafından belirlenecek. Uygulamalı sınavlar dışında, birden fazla şubede okutulan derslerin sınavlarının ortak yapılması esas olacak. Sınav sonuçları şube ve sınıf bazında analiz edilecek. Öğrenme eksikliği tespit edilen öğrencilerin durumları öğretmenler ve ilgili zümreler tarafından yeniden değerlendirilecek. Ortak yazılı sınavlarda yeni kurallar Bakanlık tarafından belirlenen sınıf düzeyleri ve derslerde ülke genelinde ortak yazılı sınav yapılabilecek. Bu sınavların hangi sınıflarda ve hangi derslerden gerçekleştirileceği öğretim yılı başında duyurulacak. Bakanlığın ülke genelinde ortak yapılmasına karar verdiği sınavlar dışında kalan sınavlar, okul genelinde ortak yazılı sınav olarak gerçekleştirilecek. Ortak yazılı sınavların soruları, konu ve soru dağılım tablolarına göre hazırlanacak. Bakanlık her dönem için bu tabloları yayımlayacak. Ülke genelinde yapılan ortak yazılı sınavlar hariç, okullardaki tüm sınavlar öğrencilerin cevaplarını kendilerinin oluşturduğu, farklı bilişsel düzeylerdeki kazanımları ölçen yazılı yoklama şeklinde yapılacak. Türkçe ve yabancı dil sınavları nasıl yapılacak? Türkçe, Türk dili ve edebiyatı ile yabancı dil derslerinin sınavları; dinleme, konuşma, okuma ve yazma becerilerini ölçmek amacıyla hem yazılı hem de uygulamalı olarak gerçekleştirilecek. Bu derslerde ülke genelinde ortak yazılı sınav yapılması halinde uygulamalı sınav okul tarafından gerçekleştirilecek ve iki sınav birlikte değerlendirilecek. Kaynaştırma ve bütünleştirme yoluyla eğitimlerine devam eden öğrencilerin ölçme ve değerlendirme süreçlerinde ise Bireyselleştirilmiş Eğitim Programı (BEP) esas alınacak. Öğrencilerin becerileri düzenli olarak izlenecek Yönetmelikle ulusal ve uluslararası izleme araştırmalarına ilişkin esaslar da belirlendi. Yeni düzenlemeyle sınav sorularının hazırlanması ve değerlendirilmesinde yapay zeka araçları kullanılabilecek. Ortak yazılı sınavlara ilişkin kurallar da yeniden belirlendi. İlkokullarda sınav yapılmayacak Yönetmelikte öne çıkan düzenlemelerden biri okul öncesi ve ilkokullara ilişkin oldu. Bu eğitim kademelerinde herhangi bir ad altında sınav yapılamayacak. Öğrencilerin bilişsel, fiziksel, sosyal ve duygusal gelişimleri eğitim süreci boyunca takip edilecek ve desteklenecek. items.articleText: Microsoft'ta küresel kesinti: 7 soruda Outlook ve Teams krizinin perde arkası - Microsoft'un Outlook ve Teams başta olmak üzere birçok hizmetinde yaşanan küresel kesinti, 70'ten fazla ülkede iş hayatını ve kamu hizmetlerini aksattı. Teknoloji devi kesinti nedeniyle özür dilerken, hizmetlerin tamamen ne zaman normale döneceğine ilişkin tarih veremedi. Dünyanın en büyük teknoloji şirketlerinden Microsoft'un bulut tabanlı hizmetlerinde yaşanan kesinti, küresel çapta milyonlarca kullanıcıyı etkiledi. Hastanelerden mahkemelere, hükümet kurumlarından küçük işletmelere kadar birçok kuruluşun faaliyetleri etkilendi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle Microsoft, sorunların başlamasından yaklaşık 24 saat sonra hizmetlerde toparlanma görüldüğünü açıklarken, kesintinin nedenine ilişkin de bilgi verdi. Yaşanan kriz, dünyanın büyük teknoloji şirketlerine olan bağımlılığını yeniden gündeme taşıdı. Microsoft'ta küresel kesinti neden yaşandı? Microsoft, kesintinin bir ağ kapasitesi yükseltmesi sırasında ortaya çıkan teknik sorundan kaynaklandığını açıkladı. Şirket, yaşanan aksaklığın bir siber saldırıdan veya yapay zeka ajanlarıyla bağlantılı bir sorundan kaynaklanmadığını belirtti. Microsoft, perşembe günü ilk olarak Amerika kıtasındaki kullanıcıların Exchange Online posta kutularına erişim sorunları yaşadığını duyurdu. Kısa süre sonra ise sorunun Microsoft 365 hizmetlerini küresel çapta etkileyebileceği uyarısında bulundu. Hangi Microsoft hizmetleri etkilendi? Kesintiden başta Outlook ve Teams olmak üzere Microsoft 365 bünyesindeki çeşitli hizmetler etkilendi. Kullanıcılar e-posta gönderme ve alma, çevrim içi toplantılara katılma ve kurumsal iletişim sistemlerine erişme konusunda sorunlar yaşadı. Dünya genelinde 430 milyondan fazla kişinin kesintiden etkilenen Microsoft ürünlerini kullandığı belirtilirken, bu kullanıcıların ne kadarının doğrudan erişim sorunu yaşadığına ilişkin net bir sayı paylaşılmadı. Kesinti hangi ülkelerde ve sektörlerde etkili oldu? Microsoft'un yaşadığı teknik sorun 70'ten fazla ülkede hissedildi. Kesinti yalnızca bireysel kullanıcıları değil, kamu kurumlarını ve kritik hizmetleri de etkiledi. Japonya hükümeti, Filipinler Yüksek Mahkemesi ve Avustralya istihbarat teşkilatı kesintiden etkilenen kurumlar arasında yer aldı. İngiltere'de bazı hastaneler, aile hekimleri, okullar ve polis teşkilatları da erişim sorunları yaşadı. Kanada'da ulusal demiryolu ağı, yolcuların seyahatlerine ilişkin e-posta bildirimlerini alamayabileceğini duyurdu. ABD'de ise Temsilciler Meclisi çalışanları, Outlook'a erişilememesi nedeniyle yasama çalışmalarının bir gün boyunca aksadığını bildirdi. Singapur ve Hindistan'da da kamu hizmetleri ve iş dünyasında çeşitli aksaklıklar meydana geldi. Outlook ve Teams ne zaman tamamen düzelecek? Microsoft, kesintinin başlamasının ardından mühendislerinin hizmetleri yeniden devreye almak için çalıştığını açıkladı. Cuma sabahı dünyanın bazı bölgelerinde kısmi iyileşme sağlandığını bildiren şirket, öğleden sonra Kuzey Amerika'da daha geniş kapsamlı toparlanma, Avrupa'nın büyük bölümünde kalıcı iyileşme ve Asya Pasifik bölgesinde olumlu gelişmeler kaydedildiğini duyurdu. Microsoft, sorunun büyüklüğü nedeniyle hizmetleri kademeli olarak yeniden devreye aldığını ve sistemlerin istikrarlı şekilde çalışmasını sağlamayı hedeflediğini belirtti. Ancak şirket, hizmetlerin tamamen normale dönmesi için henüz bir tarih veremedi. Microsoft kesintiyle ilgili ne açıklama yaptı? Microsoft, küresel kesintinin müşterileri ve iş ortakları üzerinde yarattığı aksaklık nedeniyle özür diledi. Şirket sözcüsü, "Bu olayın müşterilerimiz ve ortaklarımız için yarattığı aksaklıktan dolayı derin üzüntü duyuyoruz. Hizmetlerimize duydukları güvenin farkındayız ve bu sorumluluğu son derece ciddiye alıyoruz" ifadelerini kullandı. Microsoft'tan yapılan son açıklamada bireysel kullanıcılara yönelik hizmetlerinin tamamen normale döndüğünü, Microsoft 365 kurumsal hizmetlerinde ise kısmi toparlanma sağlandığını açıkladı. Teknoloji devi, kurumsal hizmetlerdeki sorunun tamamen çözülüp çözülmediğini değerlendirmeden önce kesinti sırasında biriken e-postaların iletim sürecini takip ettiğini bildirdi. Microsoft, hizmet durumu sayfasında yaptığı açıklamada, kesintinin etkisinin büyüklüğü nedeniyle ek önleyici tedbirlere ihtiyaç olup olmadığını belirlemek amacıyla sistemleri uzun süre izlemeye devam edeceğini belirtti. Uzmanlar Microsoft krizini nasıl değerlendiriyor? Uzmanlara göre küresel kesinti, işletmelerin ve kritik kamu hizmetlerinin sınırlı sayıdaki büyük teknoloji sağlayıcısına ne kadar bağımlı olduğunu bir kez daha ortaya koydu. Siber güvenlik şirketi e2e-assure'un CEO'su Rob Demain, Microsoft'un yaşadığı kesintinin birkaç büyük teknoloji sağlayıcısına olan bağımlılığın çarpıcı bir hatırlatıcısı olduğunu söyledi. Teknoloji danışmanlık şirketi Adaptavist'in saha baş teknoloji sorumlusu Matt Saunders ise geleneksel bilişim teknolojileri kriz planlarının alternatif hizmet sağlayıcılarının kullanılmasını önerdiğini, ancak günümüzde işletmelerin Microsoft gibi araçlar olmadan faaliyet göstermesinin son derece zor olduğunu belirtti. Saunders, yaşanan kesintinin ardından kuruluşların benzer durumlarda temel dijital araçlara erişemeden faaliyetlerini nasıl sürdüreceklerine ilişkin planlar hazırlamaları gerektiğini vurguladı.

Saunders, yaşanan kesintinin ardından kuruluşların benzer durumlarda temel dijital araçlara erişemeden faaliyetlerini nasıl sürdüreceklerine ilişkin planlar hazırlamaları gerektiğini vurguladı.

items.titleTr: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says
items.summaryTr: Trump will discuss the "reduction of nuclear weapons" during the unprecedented talks, a spokeswoman says.
items.articleText: Trump, Putin and Xi plan historic joint meeting in China next week, White House says - Published Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping are planning to meet on the sidelines of a summit in China next week, the White House has said. The historic meeting between the leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (Apec) summit in the southern city of Shenzhen, spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters. "The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world, whose proliferation President Trump believes is very dangerous," she said. It is understood Iran may also be discussed during the meeting of the world's biggest nuclear powers, but not Ukraine. Moscow and Beijing are yet to comment. No agreement was expected to follow the talks, an unnamed, senior American official said, according to news agencies AP and Reuters. Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit between the 21 member states. He will also take part in bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday - their fourth meeting since the US president returned to office in 2025. "President Trump will conclude his visit to China with a trilateral meeting between the president of the United States, the president of the People's Republic of China, and the president of the Russian Federation," Wales said. She said Trump's trip, which will also include attending an Association of Southeast Asian Nations (Asean) summit in the Philippines on Tuesday, would "secure historic wins to the American people and advance America's interests in the Indo Pacific". A nuclear weapons control treaty between the US and Russia expired in February, leaving the world's biggest nuclear arsenals without major guardrails and effectively marking an end to the arms control co-operation which helped to resolve the Cold War. The UN has urged both sides to agree a new framework without delay. Trump however said he could replace the deal with a better agreement which included China, which has been building up its arsenal. Former senior US officials and analysts told the BBC at the time that seeking Beijing and Moscow's co-operation could turn up major hurdles and take years. Xi separately hosted both Putin and Trump in Beijing just days apart earlier this year, while the US president welcomed his Chinese counterpart to Washington in September. Beijing has become a crucial trading partner for Moscow since it launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, which has isolated Russia and left it subject to Western sanctions. But a controversial US deal to import Russian diesel and the suspension of sanctions targeting the biggest buyers of Moscow's oil and gas - including China - heightened European concern about the Trump administration's softening towards the Kremlin last month. Trump and Xi have meanwhile sought to project warmer ties at summits in Beijing and Washington this year - though little significant progress appeared to have been made on key issues such as trade, their race for AI dominance, and Taiwan. The war in Iran has also been a sticking point, with Beijing the largest buyer of Tehran's oil and its biggest trade partner. Chinese state media reported on Friday that Xi would take part in "bilateral" talks on the sidelines of the Apec summit, citing a foreign ministry spokesman, but has not reported on the trilateral meeting. Earlier this month, Russian state news agency Tass reported that Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov had said there were "signals confirming readiness" for such talks at the summit. - Published20 May - Published19 May

items.articleText: ABD'de hava trafiği neden durdu? 4 soruda büyük uçuş krizi ABD'de hava trafik kontrol sistemlerinde yaşanan teknik arıza nedeniyle ülke genelinde uçuşlar dört saatten fazla durduruldu. 10 binden fazla uçuşun aksadığı kriz sonrası gecikme ve iptallerin hafta sonu da sürmesi bekleniyor. İşte 4 soruda ABD'deki uçuş krizinin nedenleri ve son durum. ABD'de 11 Eylül 2001 saldırılarından bu yana ikinci kez ülke genelinde uçuş kalkışları durduruldu. Hava trafik kontrol sistemlerinde yaşanan teknik arıza nedeniyle 10 binden fazla uçuş aksarken, yüz binlerce yolcunun seyahat planı altüst oldu. Uçuşlar yeniden başlasa da gecikme ve iptallerin hafta sonu boyunca devam etmesi bekleniyor. İşte ABD'deki hava ulaşımı krizine ilişkin merak edilenler... 1. ABD'de uçuşlar neden durduruldu? ABD Federal Havacılık İdaresi (FAA), birden fazla hava trafik kontrol merkezini etkileyen telekomünikasyon sorunları nedeniyle cuma günü ülke genelinde uçuş kalkışlarını durdurdu. ABD Ulaştırma Bakanı Sean Duffy, hava trafik kontrol sistemlerinde kullanılan telekomünikasyon yönlendiricilerinin aşırı veri yükü nedeniyle çöktüğünü açıkladı. Arızanın, uçakların yüksek irtifalarda rotaları boyunca yönlendirilmesini sağlayan merkezleri etkilediği belirtildi. FAA, güvenlik açısından tedbirli davranarak uçuşları durdurma kararı alırken, krizin temel nedenlerinden biri olarak ABD'nin eskiyen havacılık teknolojisi gösterildi. 2. Kaç uçuş ve yolcu etkilendi? Ülke genelinde dört saatten fazla süren uçuş durdurma kararı nedeniyle 10 binden fazla uçuş aksadı. Uçuş verileri şirketi Cirium'a göre, cuma günü ABD'nin doğu saatiyle 16.00'dan sonra ülkedeki havalimanlarından yaklaşık 11 bin uçuşun kalkması planlanıyordu. Bu uçuşlarda toplam 1,5 milyon yolcunun seyahat etmesi öngörülüyordu. Cirium ayrıca yaklaşık 600 uçuşun rotasında değişiklik yapıldığını, bunlardan 104'ünün farklı havalimanlarına yönlendirildiğini bildirdi. Havalimanlarında yoğunluk yaşanırken, uçakların park edileceği alanların bulunmasında da güçlük çekildi. 3. Uçuşlar yeniden başladı mı, gecikmeler ne zaman bitecek? FAA, ülke genelindeki uçuş durdurma kararını cuma günü ABD'nin doğu saatiyle 20.15'te (Türkiye saatiyle cumartesi 04.15) kaldırdı. Ancak uçuşların yeniden başlamasıyla birlikte havalimanlarındaki yoğunluk sona ermedi. Uçuş ekiplerinin günlük çalışma sürelerinin dolması, uçakların planlanan noktalara ulaşamaması ve biriken seferler nedeniyle gecikme ve iptallerin hafta sonuna, hatta daha uzun bir süreye yayılması bekleniyor. CNBC'nin ulaştığı bir şirket içi nota göre JetBlue Airways, Avrupa rotaları dışındaki cuma günü kalan uçuşlarını ve cumartesi günü planlanan bazı seferlerini iptal etme kararı aldı. 4. Siber saldırı mı, eskiyen teknoloji mi? Kriz yeniden yaşanabilir mi? ABD İç Güvenlik Bakanı Markwayne Mullin, yaşanan sorunun ülkeye yönelik bir tehdit oluşturduğuna ilişkin herhangi bir işaret bulunmadığını açıkladı. Mullin, olayın siber saldırıdan ziyade teknik bir arızadan kaynaklanmış gibi göründüğünü belirtti. ABD'de hava trafik kontrol sistemlerinin eskiyen altyapısı ve personel eksikliği uzun süredir tartışılıyor. Eylül ayında bir fiber optik kablonun yanlışlıkla kesilmesi yüzlerce uçuşu aksatırken, 2025 yılında Newark Liberty Uluslararası Havalimanı'nda yaşanan ekipman arızası da ciddi gecikmelere neden olmuştu. Ulaştırma Bakanı Duffy, mevcut altyapının arızalanmaya devam edeceği uyarısında bulunarak Kongre'den modernizasyon çalışmaları için daha fazla finansman talep etti. FAA teknisyenlerinin ise son arızaya ilişkin incelemeleri sürüyor.

items.title: What we know about the longest ground stop since 9/11
items.summary: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack or a Microsoft outage.
items.verification: Editoryal haber; resmî duyuru olarak değerlendirilmemeli
items.titleTr: What we know about the longest ground stop since 9/11
items.summaryTr: US officials say the disruption was caused by old equipment overloading and not a cyber-attack or a Microsoft outage.
items.articleText: What we know about the longest US nationwide flight ground stop since 9/11 - Published The US Federal Aviation Administration has lifted the longest nationwide ground stop of flights since the 11 September 2001 terrorist attacks. The FAA said Friday's stoppage, which lasted more than four hours, was "due to extraordinary circumstances" from a communication issue affecting all air traffic control centres. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of an attack and that everybody was safe. Here's what we know. How many flights were affected? The ground stop led to more than 8,500 delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled flights on Friday, according to FlightAware. The FAA's initial announcement at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) said all flights departing within the US would be grounded until further notice. More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air at the time. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations. Hours later, some flights were allowed to take off from San Francisco International airport. The Federal Aviation Administration opened skies again at until 20:15 EST. What about international flights? All US-bound air traffic from Eurocontrol member states was suspended "on request of the FAA due to technical issues", according to Eurocontrol's website. There are 42 Eurocontrol member states, including dozens of EU nations, the UK, Ukraine, and Turkey, as well as Israel and Morocco. Australia's largest international airport, Sydney, grounded all US-bound flights until further notice. Air Canada cancelled flights between the US and Canada. When will normal service resume? Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said in a news conference on Friday night that the outage would cause a ripple effect for a few days. "It's going to take us some time to unwind what's happened this afternoon," Duffy said. Tens of thousands of people were stranded in airports around the country, many of them "without any knowledge of where they're going to sleep tonight", Duffy said. Delta Air Lines and United Airlines said they were resuming operations. American Airlines said it was "focused on operating as many remaining flights as possible this evening". JetBlue said it would resume flights on Saturday morning. What caused the ground stop? Duffy said a legacy air traffic control communications system became overloaded. "So this is analogue telecom. Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data and they went down," Duffy said. He said this had affected communications and radar. The system needs a complete overhaul, he said, estimating a $50 billion price tag. "It's going to continue to fail," he said. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin told the news conference said they had seen "zero evidence" it was a cyber-attack. He also ruled out any link to the global Microsoft outage that began on Thursday. Mullin said the introduction of some new technology into an old air traffic control system had overwhelmed it. Both cabinet secretaries insisted the public was never in danger during the stoppage. When was the last ground stop? It was only the second such nationwide stoppage since the immediate aftermath of the al-Qaeda plane hijackings of 11 September 2001. "This looks like the worst since 9/11, but clearly not on that scale," Dr Guy Gratton, an associate professor of aviation at Cranfield University, told BBC Verify. Dr Gratton pointed to a US grounding in 2023 due to a failure in the Notice to Air Missions (Notam) system. "That lasted 1 hour and 52 minutes, delayed about 9,500 flights and cancelled about 1,300," he said. The 2023 outage meant air traffic safety notices could no longer be published, and flights were grounded until that system was restored. But Friday's incident lasted longer than the 2023 event.

items.title: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?

items.titleTr: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion?
items.summaryTr: Jojo was poached as an infant and grew up in captivity. His keepers want to find him a friend - but it's not straightforward.
items.articleText: Jojo the gorilla has spent his life alone. Can he finally find a companion? - Published In 2015, a young male gorilla named Jojo took his first tentative steps onto grass. Until that moment, the 11-year-old ape had spent almost his entire life in a tiny cage at a private zoo in Gabon, after being taken from the wild as an infant. His family had been killed by the poachers who took him. More than a decade later, Jojo is settled into a sanctuary – but he still lives alone. He hasn't had a family since he was taken, or indeed any gorilla friends. Jojo's carers at the Lekedi Foundation in Gabon want to find a companion - possibly another rescued or zoo-bred gorilla – that Jojo could live and bond with. But finding him a friend - and bringing them into his life - is not straightforward. "He's probably the most extreme case of isolation I've ever seen in a great ape," says Prof Gillian Forrester from the University of Sussex, who is studying Jojo as part of research into great ape psychology and how to help rescued animals recover from trauma. Jojo was less than a year old – an infant clinging to his mother – when he was captured and sold. Most gorillas spend the first 14 to 19 years of their life in an embedded family unit but he was kept completely alone and on public display at the private zoo that bought him. Maxe Anaclet Makaba, who is head keeper at Lekedi and sees Jojo nearly every day, says it is clear he "craves human interaction". "He will even go to the trouble of gathering leaves for us to hold, so that we [trade them] for a treat – to interact with us," he says. Jojo also calls out when women he knows well visit his enclosure and then leave, making sounds that silverback males use to summon the females in the wild, explains Éric Willaume, who runs the sanctuary. "He definitely feels lonely," he says. Jojo is one of the more than 6,000 African primates estimated to have been bought or sold in the global trade of apes and other primates between 2000 and 2023. Thousands more are trafficked illegally for use as exotic pets, wild meat, and traditional medicine, the Pan African Sanctuary Alliance says., external Experts believe when baby great apes are taken from their group at a young age like Jojo, they are left traumatised. "If they're old enough to understand what happened to them, to understand their family was killed, they just lose the will to live," explains conservationist Tony King, from UK charity the Aspinall Foundation. "You see it in their eyes – the light goes out. I never knew where that expression came from, but I've seen it in gorillas." King – who specialises in rehabilitating rescued great apes – remembers rescuing two infant sister gorillas who were brought to a sanctuary in the Congo Basin. "They were clinging to each other," he says. "They stayed together in a little tight ball for about three days before they sort of unravelled. I think that's what kept them alive." African charity the Gorilla Rehabilitation and Conservation Education (Grace) Center uses what it calls "gorilla-led" rehabilitation. When the team rescues a young gorilla from the pet trade, they put it with a group as soon as possible so they can socialise and essentially learn to be a gorilla. But Jojo's case is unusual. He is fully mature and showing signs of harmful, chronic stress, according to Forrester. In a game-changing approach to studying anxiety and trauma in apes, she has used a thermal camera to film Jojo's face. This allows her to monitor blood flow, revealing what appears to be a chronically cold nose. It's a sign of a malfunctioning stress response. When any primate – a human, chimp or gorilla - is stressed, blood flow to the eyes and ears increases. It puts them on high alert for danger, but leaves their nose, temporarily, colder. For Jojo, this "nasal dip" as it is known, does not seem to recover. "Being connected to others is incredibly important to our psychology as great apes," Forrester says. "Having another individual to share his life with would be so healing for him. "I would assume other gorillas would help him process this grief and trauma." Dr Katie Fawcett, from the Grace Center, says it's also "essential" for an animal to form social relationships to be considered for release into the wild - which is the ultimate goal for Jojo's keepers. The bonds between gorillas – what we would call friendship - is key to their society, adds Dr Robin Morrison from the University of Zurich, who studies the social lives of mountain gorillas. In one recent study, she discovered that female mountain gorillas would seek out females they knew, even if they hadn't seen them for many years, when joining a group. And she says a big part of a gorilla's normal social life is "just sitting together quietly sharing space". But Jojo has never been given the opportunity to sit quietly with another gorilla. No one knows how Jojo will react to a companion. Moving an animal from an accredited zoo would be a decision for an international committee and based on genetics, health and the animals' personalities and compatibility. Any introduction to another animal would be done very carefully – perhaps giving them an object that smells of the other before they see each other. These slow, cautious ape introductions do happen – when an animal moves from one zoo group to another, for example. Forrester has contacted a number of accredited zoos to explore the possibility of doing this for Jojo. But those discussions have fizzled out with no sign of progress. The problem, she says, is "there aren't clear processes in place to do these kinds of trans-locations". The international rules and processes for moving captive gorillas across international borders - from one zoo or safari park to another - are designed for breeding programmes. "They're not designed for reintroductions into the wild, or to find companions for animals that might need them," says Forrester. And because Jojo, who is probably in his 20s, has reached maturity, King thinks it might be too late for him to bond with other gorillas. "Jojo's situation is unique, but he is probably best where he is," King says, adding that introducing him to another animal could, somewhat ironically, be a source of more stress for him. Being alone is also natural, even relatively common, for mature male gorillas. According to Morrison, about a third of adult males are solitary. "When they reach adolescence, they tend to disperse and spend a good chunk of their life on their own." Solo males will try to persuade females to form a group with them, but some don't succeed and may feel lonely as a consequence, Morrison believes. "If we think of loneliness in an evolutionary context - this mismatch between the social interactions they want and the social interactions they're getting. I suspect feeling lonely is part of the natural, evolutionary drive to attract females." But while those phases – of family life and adult solitude - play a role in wild gorilla society, Jojo was forced into solitary confinement as an infant. Morrison believes Jojo is probably both traumatised and lonely. "[In the wild] gorillas move together, find food together, sleep together," she says. "So much of their lives is just being with this group." That is what Jojo's keepers, Forrester, and others want for Jojo. A friend. Maybe a female, or a compatible male. "It would be good for him to have a companion," says keeper Makaba. "Because being alone is like being cut off from the world - it's like being in prison. "Having another gorilla there would be a good thing for him." Related topics - Published20 April 2025 - Published7 January

items.summary: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.

items.titleTr: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test
items.summaryTr: Elon Musk’s company aborted an attempted catch of the rocket’s booster - instead it came down in the ocean.
items.articleText: Setback for SpaceX Starship rocket's double-catch test - Published SpaceX aborted its attempt to catch the bottom part of its huge Starship rocket during its latest test flight. The aim was to catch it using the mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on the launch tower as it returned to Earth, but instead it was diverted to the ocean, bursting into flames as it came down. The top part of the rocket is now continuing its journey to space, and SpaceX will decide whether it will try to catch this rocket stage at about 15:15 local time (21:15 GMT) on Saturday. It is the company's first attempt to fully recover its rocket, paving the way for making Starship fully reusable so it can fly repeatedly and reduce costs. The 124m-tall rocket successfully blasted off from the Starbase launchpad in Boca Chica, Texas at 16:45 local time (22:45 GMT) on Friday. It was supposed to catch the bottom part of the rocket - the Super Heavy booster - six and a half minutes later when it returned to the launch tower, but instead it was diverted to the ocean. During a stream of the launch, a SpaceX spokesperson said: "Safety is always the number one priority, and we're still testing out things that we haven't done before on these vehicles, and so we are prioritising making sure that we can perform each maneuver safely." The top part of the rocket, called the Ship, is continuing its journey to space, where it is deploying 26 satellites. These will form part of the Starlink constellation that provides high-speed internet from space. The Ship is due to complete 14 orbits around the Earth before returning to the launch tower 22.5 hours after taking off, where a second catch may be attempted. SpaceX has managed to catch the Super Heavy Booster on three earlier test flights. But the upper stage of the rocket, which only reached orbit for the first time in September, has never been grabbed by the chopsticks. Instead, it has splashed down in the ocean. Before the flight, SpaceX said it would only decide to try to catch the Ship after carefully assessing the vehicle while it is in space. If any problems are detected, there are various points during the flight when the rocket stage can be brought down in the ocean. Building a fully reusable rocket is a long-held ambition for SpaceX. In 2015, it became the first company to vertically land part of a rocket with its Falcon 9 booster. Falcon 9 rockets now fly more than 100 times a year, and the ability to reuse the bottom part of the rocket has dramatically cut the costs of launch. But landing an entire Starship rocket could take this to the next level, says Prof Malcolm Macdonald, president of Royal Aeronautical Society. "Full reusability has the potential to fundamentally change the economics of accessing space," he said. "One successful flight will not prove that model, but it could mark an important transition: from demonstrating that Starship can fly, to demonstrating how Starship could operate." - What is Nasa's Artemis III mission? And what comes next? - Published27 October - Watch: From launch to fiery splashdown, SpaceX's Starship completes orbit test - Published28 September After SpaceX went public earlier this year, its shareholders will be carefully monitoring this flight, as will the US Space Agency. The progress of Starship has direct implications for Nasa's attempt to land humans on the Moon in 2028 - a highly ambitious timeline. SpaceX has been given a Nasa contract to configure the Ship into a lander that will eventually take astronauts down to the lunar surface. But it is not the only company working with the US Space Agency. Blue Origin, owned by rival tech billionaire Jeff Bezos, also has a contract to use its New Glenn rocket and lander for the Moon touch down. Both companies will also play a key role in Artemis III, which is currently planned for summer 2027- another challenging schedule. This mission will see four astronauts in Nasa's Orion spacecraft attempt to dock with both SpaceX and Blue Origin's landers. Starship will need to make a lot of progress in the coming months to meet these commitments - the pace of the rocket's development has been far slower than SpaceX had intended. But Blue Origin also has much work to do. The company suffered a major setback earlier this year when its rocket exploded, totally destroying its launchpad in Florida. Blue Origin had said they would be back in action by the end of this year, but a return to flight has now been delayed to early in 2027. Nasa is under pressure to meet its timelines. Its administrator Jared Isaacman has said America is in a race with China to get to the Moon. China plans to land its Taikonauts on the lunar surface by 2030.

items.titleTr: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
items.summaryTr: The collision leaves 32 people in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
items.articleText: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision - Published Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel, Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference that all credit in the rescue effort went to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision came in around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans Chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to Port of New Orleans. Passengers began disembarking from the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping on to its side, Mayor Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help and officials shut down the Mississippi River for the search effort. The American Heritage was finishing an eight-day cruise to Mississippi River destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi. President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue was an "incredible job". Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin said the US Coast Guard also supported local rescue operations. Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what happened. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he saw the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he saw passengers and crew members "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks.

items.titleTr: After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty
items.summaryTr: A new wave of youth dissent swept India this summer, fuelled by frustration and irreverent online satire.
items.articleText: After a summer win, India's Gen Z protesters face a winter of uncertainty - Published Cheers erupted at Delhi's Jantar Mantar protest site in July as news broke that Gen-Z protests had forced federal education minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign. One protester turned to me, beaming: "This is the youth's victory." Just over three months later, the mood has shifted dramatically. Student protesters are now struggling even to assemble. Demonstrations by the Gen Z-led Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) last month over voting rights were met with sweeping restrictions and thousands of peaceful protesters were detained. The summer had seen a new wave of dissent in India, driven by deep frustration among the youth and fuelled by irreverent online satire. The movement spread across the country, and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a leader with a strongman image, unaccustomed to open criticism or mockery, struggled to contain it. But the government's increasingly forceful security response suggests it has learned from its rare concession to protesters, invoking public order to curb dissent. The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) national spokesperson Syed Zafar Islam rejected accusations of heavy-handedness and told the BBC: "The right to protest and freedom of expression is mandated by the constitution, but it has to be done within the law. It cannot override the rights of others, at the cost of public security". This is by no means the first time the Modi government has faced large-scale protests. But the breadth of them pose a challenge for the BJP, according to Yamini Aiyar, former president of the Centre for Policy Research and visiting professor at Brown University. "They are not defined by caste, gender or economic class," Aiyar said. "Even some of the core BJP base, the upwardly mobile, lower-income classes, were attracted by the movement." The scale of the youth protests is also magnified by its online presence. Protesters have broken a longstanding political taboo, openly mocking the prime minister online. "It's more than just laughs," said Sakhi, a student protester who identifies as they/them and affiliated with one of Delhi University's left-wing student organisations. "The fear of repercussions in other generations isn't felt as much in ours," they said. "Comedy is a new language to challenge authority." Previous protest movements posed serious challenges to Modi but were easier to dismiss as representing narrow sections of society or to label "anti-national", according to Aiyar. In 2020, farmers protesting against controversial agricultural reforms were blocked from entering Delhi, leading to months of demonstrations and, at times, clashes on the capital's borders. After a year of protests, the government abandoned the reforms. Protests against a contentious citizenship law in 2019 and 2020 are a stark reminder of the powers of the judiciary should anyone be deemed a national security threat. Student activist Umar Khalid was arrested under anti-terror laws after violent clashes in Delhi that killed 53 people, mostly Muslims. He was accused of being a "key conspirator". He has now spent more than six years in jail without his trial having begun. His partner Banojyotsna Lahiri told the BBC they have no regrets, but that the situation instilled "a kind of fear that has prevailed". "We are just looking at a very dark mesh of empty space, because we don't know when the endpoint is," Lahiri said. Khalid's latest appeal was lodged this month. Aiyar believes opponents are using a familiar "playbook" today to "de-legitimise" protests, but that it isn't resonating as convincingly. Nevertheless, the youth protests have struggled to recapture this summer's momentum. CJP leaders, including spokesperson Saurav Das, have faced repeated detentions and legal action. Das and fellow leader Ashutosh Ranka spent a week in Delhi's Tihar jail after being accused of trespassing at Jantar Mantar. The site of their summer victory has since been struck off the list of authorised protest venues, a decision being challenged in court. Protesters from other groups, including the left-wing All India Students' Association (Aisa), have also faced police action over allegations of defying orders. "We were expecting some kind of crackdown," said Das. He added that "the government has learnt a lot" since the summer. Legal experts warn the proceedings themselves can have a chilling effect. "A lot of cases can lead to acquittals, but it can take years. The process is the punishment, and that can deter protesters," said Ali Khan, an assistant professor at Lloyd Law College. The restrictions on demonstrations have become excessive, according to constitutional lawyer Vrinda Grover, who is advising the CJP. "Those who are organising the protests have repeatedly emphasised that this is non-violent," she argued. "Rights have been whittled down in the name of law and order." The BJP has rejected suggestions it is suppressing peaceful dissent. Islam told the BBC that demonstrations "cannot override the rights of other citizens just because a handful of people want to protest and be responsible for violence". Even dissenting online carries risk. Sakhi's viral social media posts have attracted targeted abuse and transphobic attacks. The BBC has seen posts threatening them with violence and rape. Sometimes, it can deter Sakhi from protesting or even make them change the way they dress. "Making people laugh can turn into being called anti-national," Sakhi said. "They want me to feel damaged," they added. They claim some of their content was removed after getting millions of views. Under India's information technology laws, the government can order platforms to block content on national security grounds. Notices on X and Instagram have shown accounts being withheld in India. CJP leaders have likened the crackdown to the 1975 Emergency, when then prime minister Indira Gandhi suspended civil liberties and jailed political opponents. Yet dissent has not been stamped out. Opposition parties have, in part, filled the void. Tens of thousands gathered in Delhi on 1 November for a rally organised by INDIA bloc, an alliance of opposition parties led by Congress, and permitted by the authorities. CJP leaders, meanwhile, insist the movement is bigger than their organisation. When Das walked out Delhi's Tihar prison on 21 October, photographs showed him smiling. "I would just say wait and watch," Das told us. "Time is on our side. We are a very young generation."

items.title: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore

items.titleTr: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore
items.summaryTr: The scandal has cast a spotlight on Singapore's success as a chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade.
items.articleText: How the Jensen Huang scandal created a headache for business-friendly Singapore - Published A major scandal involving Nvidia founder Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy based in Singapore has cast a spotlight on the city-state's success as a global chip hub - and a location for alleged illicit trade. On Thursday, Huang stepped down from the US chip giant after admitting he had an affair. He was reportedly involved with a woman named Alice Huang, who ran Singaporean data centre company Megaspeed, a major buyer of Nvidia's chips. For decades, Singapore has painstakingly cultivated a reputation as an open, business-friendly economy offering easy access to both the US and Chinese markets. With the AI boom, it has become a major hub for the trade of high-end semiconductor chips in recent years. Singapore was the second-largest billing centre globally last year for Nvidia, accounting for nearly a fifth of what the US chip giant earns. But notably, less than 1% of its earnings were for chips that actually entered Singapore, as the island acts as a hub for many Asian companies to place orders and send them elsewhere. Since 2022, when the US restricted advanced American semiconductors from being exported to China or acquired by Chinese companies, US officials have been concerned that other countries such as Singapore could be used by Chinese companies to gain access to the chips. Megaspeed is a case in point. It became the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in South East Asia and is suspected of giving backdoor access to these chips to Chinese companies via its data centres in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand. While Singapore does not prohibit the transfer of advanced AI chips to companies abroad, such moves can breach US export controls. Singapore has said that while it does not enforce "unilateral export controls imposed by other countries" it expects all companies in its jurisdiction to respect such regulations. The city-state has had some success in policing this. It has charged four companies and five individuals - including Chinese nationals - for various offences including fraud, following US concerns that Chinese AI company DeepSeek had been buying Nvidia chips from third parties in Singapore, among other places. They also tried to probe Megaspeed, but were faced with a number of difficulties. In a statement released on Thursday, the government said that since February 2025, they had been looking into whether Megaspeed and other firms had made false declarations about data servers which were purchased and exported through Singapore. The companies stated the equipment would end up in neighbouring Malaysia, but Singapore authorities suspect the equipment's final destinations were elsewhere. Singapore said it sought assistance from US authorities several times to get more information from one of the investigated companies - Supermicro, a US-based company which the BBC understands was supplying computer servers to Megaspeed. But "despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance", it said in its statement. The BBC has sought comment from the US State Department. Singapore authorities said they had also investigated Alice Huang - not for espionage, but for any possible role in Megaspeed's suspected fraud. In the end, they found "insufficient evidence" of crime and let her leave Singapore in February this year, after holding her passport for several months. Since launching their probe nearly two years ago, Singapore has yet to bring any charges against Megaspeed or any of the companies and individuals linked to the case. Singapore and US investigations into Megaspeed are still ongoing. In 2024, US officials had paid a visit to a Malaysian data centre owned by Megaspeed and saw Nvidia technology still in their boxes, raising concerns that Megaspeed was shipping high-end chips out elsewhere, according to a report by the New York Times. Last year, Megaspeed appeared to have imported 50,000 more chips than Nvidia could account for, according to a Bloomberg report. Nvidia later adjusted its own figures after visiting more warehouses. Megaspeed has maintained it has always acted lawfully and that previous inspections by authorities found no evidence of illegal activity. On Thursday, the company said it "welcomes appropriate government scrutiny" and that it is "committed to working constructively and transparently with the US government". China has also long refuted accusations that its companies and institutions are illegally obtaining high-end US chips. How Megaspeed and Alice Huang came to Singapore highlights other vulnerabilities stemming from the city-state's openness. In recent years, the city-state has become a prime destination for Chinese companies, with tech firms such as TikTok and Manus making it their global headquarters. Besides Singapore's ease of doing business, it has a population that is mostly ethnically Chinese and largely views China positively. For a Chinese firm, Singapore offers a base near the mainland and a "neutral address" that global customers and investors accept, said Winston Ma, adjunct professor at New York University's School of Law. But critics say this has given rise to "Singapore-washing", where Chinese companies use the city-state's clean image to obscure their origins, reduce suspicions and even cover up dubious activities. Washington-based security analysis group C4ADS told the BBC they had assessed Alice Huang's setup of Megaspeed to be such a case. BBC checks of corporate records in China, Hong Kong and Singapore found that in 2019, Huang sold a gaming company and its subsidiaries to Chinese gaming firm 7Road. In March 2023, a 7Road subsidiary in Singapore named Huang as its executive director. The next day it changed its name - to Megaspeed. Huang was in charge for eight months before she transferred the company to a Singaporean man. During this period, Megaspeed went through "a critical period of corporate restructuring and regional expansion", and her corporate relationships raised questions about whether "Megaspeed's Singaporean identity is genuine or effectively Chinese-controlled", according to C4ADS. Even after she transferred Megaspeed, C4ADS assessed that she was still "practically in control" of the company, based on her links to Megaspeed via another company as well as LinkedIn posts where she continued to identify herself as Megaspeed's "chairwoman" at conferences. Megaspeed has not answered BBC queries regarding the company's and Alice Huang's links to China and the Chinese government. All this reinforces the dilemma faced by Singapore. "For the longest time, Singapore has managed to enjoy the best of both worlds with excellent relations with US and China," Nanyang Technological University politics and international studies lecturer Dylan Loh said. Singapore has long positioned itself as a neutral party between the two superpowers. Its prime minister Lawrence Wong has insisted that his country is neither pro-China nor pro-America, but "pro-Singapore". But Loh says this balancing act "has now fast become very difficult to manage and sometimes quite fraught too" with the US-China dispute over chips. With the Megaspeed case, the tightrope Singapore has walked is set to get even narrower, according to analysts. Beijing may ask why Singapore is investigating issues pertaining to US restrictions and whether they are siding with the US' interests, says Chong Ja Ian, a Singaporean political scientist and non-resident scholar with Carnegie China. Washington, in turn, might read Singapore's latest statement as "pushing blame" on the US, which could lead to backlash from the White House, he said. "Singapore has made a policy position not to take sides. But by not choosing a side, they run the risk of being seen as complicit" in either side's agenda, he said. But Benjamin Ho, an assistant professor and China expert at Singapore's S Rajaratnam School of International Studies, noted that this was "not the first or last time Singapore will be caught between the US and China". "This is the price that an open economy has to grapple with - you get caught in the middle when things turn sour." Additional reporting by Jack Lau of the BBC's Global China Unit. - Published1 day ago - Published1 day ago

items.articleText: Çalışma hayatında yeni dönem! 2027-2029 Adil Geçiş Planı yayımlandı - Türkiye'nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda hazırlanan Ulusal Adil Geçiş Stratejisi ve Eylem Planı, Cumhurbaşkanlığı Genelgesi ile yürürlüğe girdi. - Plan kapsamında çalışanların yeni beceriler kazanması, istihdamın korunması ve dönüşümden etkilenen sektör ve bölgelerin desteklenmesi hedefleniyor. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan’ın imzasını taşıyan genelge, Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 2027-2029 dönemini kapsayan strateji, iklim değişikliği ile yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün çalışma hayatı üzerindeki etkilerini yönetmeyi amaçlıyor. Genelgede, Türkiye’nin 2053 net sıfır emisyon hedefi doğrultusunda dönüşüm sürecinin kimseyi geride bırakmadan yürütülmesinin önemine dikkat çekildi. 2 Temmuz 2025 tarihli İklim Kanunu ile mevzuata giren adil geçiş yaklaşımının; çalışanların ve işletmelerin değişen koşullara uyum sağlamasını, yeni beceriler kazanmasını, insana yakışır işlerin artırılmasını ve sosyal korumanın güçlendirilmesini gerektirdiği belirtildi. Üç temel politika ekseni belirlendi Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı koordinasyonunda, ilgili paydaşların katılımıyla hazırlanan strateji üç temel eksene dayanıyor: Beceri uyumu: Çalışanların dönüşen iş gücü piyasasının ihtiyaçlarına uygun beceriler kazanması. Kapsayıcı dönüşüm: Yeşil ve dijital dönüşümün farklı sektör, bölge ve toplumsal gruplar üzerindeki etkilerinin gözetilmesi. Sosyal koruma ve toplumsal dayanıklılık: Dönüşüm sürecinde çalışanların ve toplumun desteklenmesi. Plan kapsamında öncelikli sektörlere yönelik sektörel politikalar da uygulanacak. Uygulama altı ayda bir raporlanacak Strateji ve Eylem Planı, Çalışma ve Sosyal Güvenlik Bakanlığı'nın resmi internet sitesinde yayımlanacak. Planın koordinasyon, izleme ve değerlendirme çalışmaları ilgili kamu kurumları ve sosyal tarafların katılımıyla Bakanlık tarafından yürütülecek. Eylem Planı'nda sorumlu olarak belirlenen kurum ve kuruluşlar, uygulamadaki gelişmeleri altı aylık dönemler halinde Bakanlığa bildirecek. items.articleText: Sözleşmeli personele yeni dönem! Disiplin cezalarından izinlere birçok kural değişti - Kamuda 4/B statüsünde görev yapan sözleşmeli personeli ilgilendiren yeni düzenleme Resmi Gazete’de yayımlandı. - Disiplin cezalarından hastalık izinlerine, göreve başlama sürelerinden kurum içi yer değişikliklerine kadar birçok konuda yeni kurallar getirildi. Cumhurbaşkanı Recep Tayyip Erdoğan'ın imzasıyla yayımlanan 11982 sayılı Cumhurbaşkanı Kararı, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihli Resmi Gazete'de yürürlüğe girdi. CNBCE.COM'u öncelikli haber kaynağınız olarak ekleyin Ekle 657 sayılı Devlet Memurları Kanunu'nun 4/B maddesi kapsamında çalışan sözleşmeli personelin çalışma koşullarını düzenleyen kararla mevcut esaslarda değişiklik yapıldı. Sözleşmeli personele disiplin cezaları uygulanacak Yeni düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin disipline aykırı fiil ve davranışlarında devlet memurlarına uygulanan disiplin hükümlerinin kıyasen uygulanması kararlaştırıldı. Buna göre disiplin cezalarının belirlenmesi, yetkili merciler ve disiplin kurullarının işleyişinde memurlara ilişkin hükümler esas alınacak. Aylıktan kesme cezası ise personelin pozisyonuna bağlı ödemelerin toplamı üzerinden 1/30 ile 1/8 arasında uygulanabilecek. Kademe ilerlemesinin durdurulması ve daha ağır cezaları gerektiren fiillerde disiplin kurulu kararı alınacak. Personelin görevine, atamaya yetkili amirin onayıyla son verilebilecek. Hastalık izinleri ve rapor süreleri değişti Hastalık ve refakat izinlerinde, 657 sayılı Kanun'un 105'inci maddesindeki ilgili hükümler sözleşmeli personele de uygulanacak. SGK tarafından ödenen geçici iş göremezlik ödeneği ise personelin ücretinden düşülecek. Azami hastalık izni süresinin tamamlanmasının ardından göreve başlanmaması da sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine ilişkin hükümler arasına eklendi. Göreve başlama sürelerine sınır getirildi Yeni kurallara göre aynı yerde göreve başlayacak personelin, tebliği izleyen iş günü içinde işe başlaması gerekecek. Başka bir yerde görevlendirilen personel ise tebliğ tarihinden itibaren 15 günü izleyen iş günü içinde görevine başlayacak. Belgeyle ispatlanabilen zorlayıcı nedenler dışında bu sürelere uyulmaması, sözleşmenin sona erdirilmesine neden olabilecek. Kurum içi yer değişikliğinde 3 yıl şartı 4/B kapsamında çalışan personelin kurum içi yer değişiklikleri de yeniden düzenlendi. Buna göre personelin işe başladığı tarihten itibaren aynı kurumda üç yıllık çalışma süresini tamamlayana kadar yapacağı yer değişikliklerinde belirlenen özel usul ve esaslar uygulanacak. Sözleşmeli personelin görevden uzaklaştırılmasında da devlet memurlarına ilişkin hükümler kıyasen geçerli olacak. Memur kadrosuna geçenlerin boş pozisyonları iptal edilecek Sözleşmeli personelin memur kadrosuna atanması halinde boşalan sözleşmeli personel pozisyonları, başka bir işleme gerek kalmaksızın iptal edilmiş sayılacak. İptal edilen pozisyonlar ilgili kamu personel bilgi sistemine bildirilecek. Eğitim ve ücret ödemelerinde yeni hükümler Düzenlemeyle sözleşmeli personelin temel eğitim, hazırlayıcı eğitim ve staj süreçlerinin görev yaptıkları kurumlar tarafından yürütülmesi kararlaştırıldı. Hizmet içi eğitimlerle personelin mesleki gelişiminin desteklenmesi de öngörüldü. Ücretlerin ay başında peşin ödenmesi uygulaması devam edecek. Ancak ay sonundan önce görevden ayrılan personelden kalan günlere ilişkin ödemeler geri alınacak. Memur kadrosuna atananlar, kendisine aylık bağlananlar ve hayatını kaybeden personel bu uygulamanın dışında tutulacak. Yeni düzenleme, 14 Kasım 2026 tarihinde yayımlanmasıyla yürürlüğe girdi.

items.summaryTr: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
items.articleText: Here’s what happened in crypto today Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation. Today in crypto, OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT, Jane Street nearly eightfold its Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings while trimming its BlackRock stake, and Trump nominated four SEC and CFTC commissioners, including a replacement for Hester Peirce. OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said. The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction. The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. Jane Street boosts Fidelity Bitcoin ETF holdings nearly 8x, trims IBIT Jane Street’s share count in Fidelity’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) rose nearly eightfold in the third quarter, while its holdings in BlackRock’s fund fell 19%. The trading giant ended September with 7.01 million shares of Fidelity Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC0, up from about 887,000 at the end of June. The position was worth $509 million on Sept. 30, according to its second-quarter and third-quarter filings. Jane Street’s holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT) fell to 20.22 million shares from 24.88 million. A higher share price lifted the reported value of its stake to $957 million from $828 million. Jane Street was the largest reported institutional holder of BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of June after boosting its share count by 324% in Q2, according to 13F Pro. IBIT is the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF with $56 billion in net assets as of Thursday. The firm also added nearly 9 million shares (about $249 million) of the ARK 21Shares Bitcoin ETF (ARKB), while more than doubling its holdings in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust ETF (ETHA) by 7.83 million shares (about $158 million). Trump nominates Hester Peirce successor among SEC, CFTC picks US President Donald Trump has nominated Steven Levine to replace former Securities and Exchange Commission Commissioner Hester Peirce, one of the agency’s most prominent crypto advocates, as part of four nominations to fill vacancies at the SEC and Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The White House’s latest announcement on Thursday named two nominees each for the SEC and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, agencies whose decisions help shape US cryptocurrency regulation, among other functions. All four nominations require Senate confirmation. The nominations would replenish several commissioner roles. The SEC currently has only two of its five commissioner seats filled, while CFTC Chairman Michael Selig is the sole member of his agency’s five-seat commission. The nominations come weeks before Democrats are set to take control of the Senate in January, giving a narrow window for Republicans to confirm Trump’s picks.

items.articleText: OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex OpenAI’s new payment wallet lets AI agents complete purchases using existing card networks, with plans to eventually allow preauthorized transactions. OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa. The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said. The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction. The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems. OpenAI joins a growing field of companies developing payment systems for AI agents. Google introduced its Agent Payments Protocol in 2025, while Visa and Mastercard have launched initiatives to support AI-initiated transactions. Crypto companies are also developing payment infrastructure for AI agents. Coinbase introduced its x402 protocol in 2025, enabling autonomous stablecoin payments for digital services, while Circle launched its Agent Stack in May, allowing agents to hold and spend USDC within predefined limits. Crossmint, which provides stablecoin infrastructure, has taken a different approach, combining stablecoin wallets with traditional card networks. Global agentic commerce transaction value is expected to reach $1.5 trillion by 2030, according to an April report from Juniper Research, up from an estimated $8 billion in 2026.
